subject: blackpoll warbler
title: A Bird Lighter Than Three Coins Flies 3 Days Over the Ocean Nonstop

scenes.text: This songbird weighs twelve grams. It crosses the Atlantic without stopping once.
Every autumn the blackpoll warbler leaves New England and heads straight out over open ocean.
Tracked birds flew up to two thousand seven hundred seventy kilometres in up to three days.
No landing, no food, no water. There's nowhere to stop.
How? Before leaving, it nearly doubles its body weight in fat, burned as fuel on the way.
It lands in the Caribbean, refuels, and keeps going to South America.

description:
The blackpoll warbler, a songbird of about 12 grams, flies up to 2,770 km nonstop over the Atlantic from northeastern North America to the Caribbean in up to three days (Biology Letters, 2015).
Scientists tracked it with geolocators weighing half a gram; before departing it nearly doubles its body weight.
Which animal journey amazes you most?
first_comment: In spring it takes the long way home over land, so the ocean crossing happens only once a year. Could you go three days without stopping for anything?
